full_judgment: 3. Defendant No. 8, respondent No. 1, contested the suit contending that the transaction under the Kabala dated June 9, 1945 between Prohllad Chandra Sen and the Bank was not an out and out sale but was a mortgage on conditional sale, that the plaintiff's predecessor by the subsequent sale-deed dated August 22, 1953 did not acquire valid title and that the Bank went into liquidation in July 1957 in which connection a winding up proceeding being Matter No. 7 of 1957 started. It was further contended that the Liquidator of the Bank, namely, the then State Bank of Pakistan, reconvened the suit land to the sons of Prohllad by executing a registered sale-deed dated June 1, 1960, that one day thereafter the sons of Prohallad sold the land to defendant No. 8 by a registered kabala date June 2, 1960 on the basis on which dsfendant No. 8 got title and went into possession of the land. But the suit was decreed by the trial court on March 13, 1962 and this decree was confirmed by the Additional District Judge in appeal on August 25, 1964. As against this appellate decree the respondent filed the second appeal in which the question of jurisdiction was raised taking the ground that the winding-up proceeding which had started in 1957 was pending when the Banking Companies Ordinance came into force from July 1962 and as such the Company Judge got exclusive jurisdiction thereon. The High Court Division accepted this contention and held that the "Civil Court was definitely prohibited from exercising its jurisdiction which exclusively vested in the High Court under section 61 and decisions of these courts below were quorum-non-juice" and in that view of the matter transferred the case to the Company Judge.
